Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

mutter verb

also mumble, murmur, say under one’s breath

classical

Liv. 33.31: clam mussantēs (Lewis & Short; not in Cicero or Caesar)
Traupman 349

mussō, mussāre, mussāvī, mussātum

verb, first conjugation

mutter, murmur, speak under one’s breath

Varro derives it from the sound mū, the least a mute man can say (L.L. 7.101): rightly, an imitative word. Lewis & Short notes that it is not used by Cicero or Caesar.

Other words

  • murmurō, murmurāre — murmur, grumble

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 3.1.149: servī murmurant, of grumbling (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Nimis crūdum est hoc pōmum. — Quid tū mussās?

    This apple is too green. — What are you muttering?Vīv. Exerc. 24

SourcesLewis & Short: musso · Lewis & Short: murmuro

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 349.
